item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q002_mazg_hise_remote_homology","answer":"SCOPe 2.08 supports remote homology—probable common ancestry—between d1vmga_ and d1y6xa1. They belong to different families: d1vmga_ (SUNID 113676) is MazG-like, a.204.1.2; d1y6xa1 (SUNID 122676; chain A residues 7–93) is HisE-like (PRA-PH), a.204.1.4. Both belong to the all-alpha NTP pyrophosphatases superfamily a.204.1 (SUNID 101386), whose homology record explicitly supports homology at the superfamily level. They also share fold a.204 and class a, All alpha proteins; shared fold or class alone would not establish common ancestry.\n\nThe superfamily annotation describes an active-site module of five helices, four supplied by one subunit or structural repeat and the fifth by another. This supports a conserved structural framework, but does not establish identical substrate specificity or physiological function. SCOPe labels d1vmga_ a hypothetical Sulfolobus solfataricus protein and d1y6xa1 phosphoribosyl-ATP pyrophosphatase HisE from Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It would exceed this evidence to assign HisE activity or a histidine-biosynthesis role to d1vmga_, or MazG-like broad nucleotide specificity to d1y6xa1. Identical catalytic residues, metal requirements, kinetics, oligomerization, and functional interchangeability also cannot be inferred from superfamily membership. Such transfers require independent biochemical substrate/activity measurements, supported by active-site sequence/structure comparisons and physiological evidence. Either domain may guide a structural comparison, but neither is automatically a substrate-specific functional template for the other.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope__get_scop_domains","mcp__scope__get_scop_node","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1vmga_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1vmga_/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1y6xa1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1y6xa1/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/101386","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/101386/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/101386/homology","Pretrained knowledge of SCOPe hierarchy and limits of functional inference"]}]}
